claims.text: Ru in PtPdRhRuIrOs generates surface-bound oxygenated species at lower overpotentials under ethanol oxidation conditions.
Ru-derived oxygenated species synergistically couple with adjacent Rh and Pd sites.
The proposed Ru–Rh–Pd coupling promotes oxidation of adsorbed acetaldehyde-like intermediates.
The proposed Ru-mediated process enhances ethanol oxidation activity and selectivity.
The initial catalyst is a nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution with a uniform composition.
Ru content will be varied while the ratios among the other metals are held constant.
Operando IR and online mass spectrometry can track surface intermediates and product distributions during ethanol electro-oxidation.
The relevant operating regime includes 0.1–1 M KOH and temperatures of 60–80 °C.
Surface hydroxyl or oxo species form on Ru at lower overpotentials.
Ru-bound hydroxyl or oxo species facilitate removal of carbonaceous intermediates from adjacent Rh and Pd sites.
Neighboring Ru and ethanol-fragment adsorption sites operate through a bifunctional mechanism.
Suppressing CO and acetaldehyde-like poisoning intermediates improves catalytic performance and durability.
Increasing Ru content will decrease operando IR signals assigned to adsorbed CO.
Increasing Ru content will decrease operando IR signals assigned to acetaldehyde.
Increasing Ru content will increase CO2 formation relative to a lower-Ru or Ru-free catalyst.
A minimal-Ru or Ru-free alloy with the other components retained at nominal ratios is an appropriate baseline.
The mechanism should hold from approximately pH 7 to 14 and at temperatures up to about 80 °C because Ru can form stable surface hydroxyl species in that regime.
The strength of Ru–Rh synergy may vary with alloy morphology or pH.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as the 'same catalyst composition' while also containing minimal or no Ru. Removing or reducing Ru necessarily changes the six-metal composition, although the intended comparison can be made coherent by holding the ratios among the remaining metals and total loading constant.
